newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish markets wind down, lack incentive to trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish markets wind down, lack incentive to trade.

text.p: Irish financial markets range-traded on Tuesday in thin, pre-Christmas dealing, lacking incentive to adjust positions so close to the holiday, dealers said.
In the bond market dealers said there was little change on Monday's closing levels but they expected further convergence trade to pick up again in the New Year.

The Irish pound was equally quiet and traders said that -- while the Irish unit had drifted further below parity due to sterling's strength today -- they saw it close to its floor and expected it whould start to creep up in the New Year.
The ISEQ index of shares notched up 3.86 points to 2,671.59 but volume was light, equity dealers said.
"Many overseas markets are closed and all Irish markets will close with the stock exchange at around 1230 GMT so there is little or no change on yesterday's closing levels," one dealer said.
"Fresh convergence trade should give the market a further push in the New Year," he added.
By 1145 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was relatively unchanged at 101.50 to yield 6.03 percent and the 10-year benchmark due 2006 was 108.80, yielding 6.61 percent.
In the currency market the Irish pound drifted down to 0.9909 stg, 2.5770 marks but firmed slightly to $1.6575 from a close of 0.9922 stg, 2.5801 marks and $1.6603.
The currency dealer said the Irish unit was likely to see some volatility in the New Year until it re-established a comfortable trading level.
Economic data of note early in the New Year are domestic Central Bank credit data, due for release on January 2, and Exchequer Returns to be published on January 3.

Economists' forecasts for the Exchequer Borrowing Requirement ranges between 350-400 million punts and forecasts for credit growth are around 14.3 percent, which is unchanged on last month, to 14.5 percent.
